songInfo.title: Dust My Broom
songInfo.key: E Major (Open D tuning also common)
songInfo.tuning: Open D (DADF#AD) or Standard with slide

keyAndScale.primaryKey: E major (or D major in Open D tuning)

scalesUsed.application: Foundation for the iconic slide guitar riff and melodic phrasing

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D - E
scalesUsed.application: Blues tonality with the flatted 7th (D natural) creating dominant quality

scalesUsed.notes: E - G - A - Bb - B - D

keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C# minor (relative minor of E major)

mainProgression.description: Standard 12-bar blues form with dominant 7th chords throughout, the foundation of electric blues

sectionProgressions.description: Classic 12-bar blues with the turnaround ending on V7 to cycle back to the top
Same 12-bar form as the verse, with the slide guitar taking the lead melody

harmonicFunction: E7 (I7) - Tonic dominant chord, the home base with a blues-dominant quality
A7 (IV7) - Subdominant, provides the characteristic move to the IV chord in bars 5-6
B7 (V7) - Dominant, creates maximum tension at bar 9 and in the turnaround

techniques.name: Slide Guitar Triplet Riff
techniques.description: The legendary opening riff played with a glass or metal slide, featuring rapid triplet figures that defined the electric blues slide guitar style

notes: The riff is built on rapid triplet picking on a single string with slide
In Open D tuning: slide from the 10th to 12th fret on the high strings
In Standard tuning: played on the B and high E strings around the 12th fret area
The triplet pattern is the defining rhythmic element - three notes per beat
Slide must maintain contact with the string without pressing to the fret
sequence: Position slide over the 12th fret (or equivalent in Open D)
Pick rapid triplets on the high strings: down-up-down, down-up-down
Slide between fret positions (10-12, 12-10) while maintaining triplet rhythm
End each phrase with a slide up to the 12th fret and sustain with vibrato
Repeat the riff pattern over each chord change, adjusting position accordingly
tips: Use a glass slide for a warmer, smoother tone (Elmore James preferred glass)
Keep the slide parallel to the frets and directly over the fret wire, not between frets
Mute strings behind the slide with your trailing fingers to control noise
Practice the triplet picking pattern without the slide first to lock in the rhythm
Start at 80 BPM and build gradually - the full tempo of 160 BPM is demanding

techniques.name: 12-Bar Blues Form
techniques.description: The fundamental 12-bar blues chord structure that serves as the harmonic framework for the entire song

notes: 12 bars divided into three 4-bar phrases
Bars 1-4: I chord (E7) establishing the tonic
Bars 5-6: IV chord (A7) providing harmonic movement
Bars 7-8: Return to I chord (E7)
Bar 9: V chord (B7) for maximum tension
Bar 10: IV chord (A7) beginning resolution
Bars 11-12: I chord (E7) with V7 turnaround
sequence: Count through the 12-bar form slowly, one chord per bar
Play simple chord shapes (E7-A7-B7) through the form
Practice the turnaround (bars 11-12) which cycles back to the top
Once comfortable, add the shuffle rhythm to each chord
tips: Memorize the form by thinking in 3 phrases: statement (I), departure (IV-I), resolution (V-IV-I)
The turnaround in bar 12 is crucial for cycling back smoothly
Count each bar aloud while playing until the form is internalized
Listen to dozens of 12-bar blues songs to train your ear for the form

techniques.name: Slide Vibrato
techniques.description: Expressive vibrato technique using the slide, rocking it slightly above and below the target pitch for an emotional, singing quality

notes: Vibrato is achieved by rapidly moving the slide slightly sharp and flat of the target fret
The movement is along the length of the string (toward bridge and nut), not across strings
Width of vibrato determines expressiveness: wider for more emotional, narrower for subtler
Applied at the end of phrases and on sustained notes for blues expression
Must stay centered on the target pitch - vibrato should oscillate evenly around it
sequence: Position slide directly over the target fret wire
Sustain the note with a firm pick attack
Begin small oscillations (about 1/4 inch) back and forth along the string
Gradually widen the vibrato for more expressive moments
Control the speed: slower vibrato for mournful feel, faster for intensity
tips: Practice vibrato on a single note for minutes at a time to develop control
Use your ear: the vibrato should sound musical, not like a mistake
Keep trailing fingers behind the slide for string damping during vibrato
Listen to Elmore James recordings to internalize his specific vibrato speed and width
details.progression: Applied over any chord in the 12-bar form

sections.name: Intro (Slide Riff)
sections.description: The legendary opening slide guitar riff - rapid triplets on the high strings that became one of the most copied phrases in blues history
notes: This is the most iconic slide guitar riff in blues history
Rapid triplet figures on the high strings with the slide
The riff establishes the E tonality before the 12-bar form begins
Must be played with conviction and rhythmic precision

sections.name: Verse 1
sections.description: First 12-bar verse with vocal melody accompanied by slide guitar fills between vocal phrases, following the standard blues form
notes: Slide guitar answers the vocal phrases in call-and-response style
The triplet riff returns between vocal lines
Chord changes follow the 12-bar blues form precisely
The slide shifts position to follow each chord change

sections.name: Solo 1
sections.description: Extended slide guitar solo over the 12-bar form, showcasing Elmore James's fierce slide technique with triplets, vibrato, and string bending
notes: Solo follows the 12-bar form - the slide position shifts with each chord change
Mix of the main triplet riff and improvised slide phrases
Heavy use of vibrato on sustained notes
Raw, aggressive slide tone with maximum expression

sections.name: Verse 2
sections.description: Second verse continuing the vocal and slide guitar interplay over the 12-bar form with increasing intensity
notes: Same 12-bar structure as Verse 1 with more aggressive slide fills
Slide guitar becomes more prominent and insistent
The interplay between voice and slide intensifies
Building energy toward the final solo section

sections.name: Solo 2
sections.description: Final solo section with the most intense slide work, building to the song's emotional peak
notes: Most intense slide playing of the song
Wider vibrato and more aggressive attack
Triplet riff played at maximum ferocity
Peak emotional intensity before the outro

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Quick ending with a final statement of the slide riff resolving to the tonic E chord
notes: Quick V-I resolution to end the song
Final slide into the tonic E chord
The ending is abrupt and definitive
A final burst of the triplet riff before the resolved chord

guitar.recommended: Resonator guitar (National or Dobro style) or hollow-body electric
alternatives: Solid-body electric guitar with heavy gauge strings (.012-.054)
Any electric guitar set up for slide (higher action recommended)
guitar.pickup: Single coil or P-90 for authentic raw blues tone

amp.recommended: Small tube amp driven to natural breakup (Fender Champ, Deluxe)
alternatives: Any low-wattage tube amp at volume

settings.gain: 6-7 (natural tube breakup from volume, not preamp gain)
settings.middle: 6 (present midrange for the slide to sing)
settings.bass: 4 (controlled low end to avoid mud with slide)

effects.distortion: None - natural amp breakup from cranked volume only
effects.reverb: Light spring reverb if available on the amp
effects.other: Glass or metal slide (glass for warmer tone, metal for brighter and louder)

beginner.focus: Learn the 12-bar blues form and basic slide positioning
steps: Memorize the 12-bar blues chord form: I7-IV7-V7 in E
Practice simple E7, A7, and B7 chord shapes without slide
Get comfortable wearing a slide and producing clean, buzzing-free notes
Play single sustained notes with the slide at the 12th, 7th, and 5th frets

intermediate.focus: Develop the triplet picking pattern and basic slide phrases
steps: Practice the triplet picking pattern (down-up-down) without the slide at 80 BPM
Add the slide to the triplet pattern on a single string, sliding between frets
Learn to shift slide position for each chord change in the 12-bar form
Work on basic slide vibrato technique on sustained notes

advanced.focus: Master the full riff at tempo with authentic slide tone and expression
steps: Build the triplet riff up to full speed (160 BPM) cleanly
Develop wide, expressive slide vibrato in the style of Elmore James
Practice the call-and-response between vocal melody and slide fills
Perform the complete song with all verses and solos at tempo

commonMistakes: Pressing the slide down onto the frets instead of floating above them
Slide not positioned directly over the fret wire, causing out-of-tune notes
Neglecting to mute strings behind the slide, creating unwanted noise and overtones
Rushing the triplet pattern instead of maintaining even, steady triplet subdivisions
practiceRoutine: Spend 10 minutes on slide intonation: play single notes at the 5th, 7th, and 12th frets with a tuner
Practice the triplet picking pattern on open strings without the slide for 5 minutes
Combine slide and triplets slowly (80 BPM), playing the main riff on a single string
Work through one full 12-bar chorus with slide, focusing on smooth chord transitions
focusAreas: Slide intonation - notes must be in tune by positioning the slide precisely over fret wire
Triplet rhythm precision - all three notes of each triplet must be perfectly even
String muting behind the slide to eliminate unwanted noise and sympathetic vibrations
Vibrato control - developing wide, even vibrato for expressive sustain
metronomeWork: Practice triplet subdivisions at 80 BPM (3 notes per beat) on open strings
Build up slide riff at 100 BPM, then 120 BPM, targeting the full 160 BPM
Work on the 12-bar form with chord changes at 120 BPM before adding the slide
Practice turnaround timing at full tempo to ensure smooth cycling
